report_name: Radware Breach Exposes Customer Cloud Keys Via Public API

threat_actors.name: Unauthorized Actor
threat_actors.description: An unnamed threat actor responsible for discovering and exploiting an exposed Radware management API to exfiltrate customer data and cloud credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor discovered the exposed Radware API endpoint through internet-wide vulnerability scanning.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor accessed the unauthenticated, public-facing Radware Cloud WAF management API to enumerate and exfiltrate data.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials in Files
attack_patterns.description: The actor obtained cloud storage credentials for AWS S3 and Azure Blob, which were stored as configuration data accessible via the exposed API.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attackers began using the stolen AWS and Azure credentials to attempt unauthorized access to customer cloud storage accounts.

vulnerabilities.name: Unauthenticated API Exposure
vulnerabilities.description: A Radware internal Cloud WAF management API was exposed to the public internet without an authentication mechanism, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive customer data and cloud credentials.

identities.name: Radware
identities.description: Cybersecurity vendor that suffered a data breach on November 19, 2026, due to an exposed internal API for its Cloud WAF service, leading to the compromise of customer data and cloud credentials.

identities.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
identities.description: Cloud service provider whose customer S3 credentials were exposed and actively used by attackers following the Radware data breach.

identities.name: Microsoft Azure
identities.description: Cloud service provider whose customer Blob Storage credentials were exposed in the Radware data breach.

infrastructure.name: Exposed Radware Cloud WAF API
infrastructure.description: An internal management API for Radware's Cloud WAF service that was publicly exposed without authentication. The actor used it to query and exfiltrate customer data and cloud credentials.

indicators.name: Exposed Internal API Endpoint Detection
indicators.pattern:
title: Exposed Internal API Endpoint Detection
id: 9c5b1f3a-8d4e-4b1f-9a2d-7e8c6a5b4d3e
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests to URL paths containing keywords like 'internal' or 'admin', which may indicate exposed internal APIs that should not be public.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/radware-reports-data-breach-involving-exposed-cloud-management-api
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-26
tags:
  - attack.t1190
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains:
      - '/api/internal/'
      - '/internal/api/'
      - '/admin/api/'
      - '/api/admin/'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web requests to URL paths containing keywords like 'internal' or 'admin', which may indicate exposed internal APIs, based on hunting hints from the Radware breach report.
